title: Speech by Chairman Bernanke on communication and monetary policy - Federal Reserve Board
主要内容: On November 19, 2013, Federal Reserve Chairman Ben Bernanke emphasized the importance of transparency and communication in monetary policy during a speech at the National Economists Club Annual Dinner. He highlighted that transparency enhances public understanding and confidence, promotes informed discussion of policy options, and increases accountability of policymakers. Bernanke noted that the Fed's focus had shifted from addressing the financial crisis to supporting economic recovery post-recession. He explained that enhanced transparency is crucial for the effectiveness of monetary policy, despite the challenges of forecasting economic outcomes. The FOMC reaffirmed its 2 percent longer-term inflation goal and its best assessment of maximum employment levels, acknowledging the uncertainty and potential revisions in these assessments. The Federal Reserve Board's FOMC maintained its asset purchase pace in September 2013, consistent with earlier guidance. Despite mixed evidence on labor market gains, the decision reinforced forward rate guidance credibility, with longer-term rates falling and short-term rate expectations aligning with the guidance.
